chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a group of Muslims who were eating and a Magian man presented himself, should they invite him to their meal? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, I would not eat with the Magian, and I dislike that I should prohibit upon you something which you are doing in your cities.'

key_terms.مَجُوسِيٌّ: Magian/Zoroastrian, a type of Ahl al-Kitab
key_terms.يَأْكُلُونَ: They eat (referring to the act of dining)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for Muslims to eat with Zimmis (People of the Book) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between personal preference (*karaahat*) and legal obligation (*haram*), clarifying that his avoidance of dining with Zoroastrians was a voluntary act of piety rather than a binding prohibition for the community. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of *al-urf* (local custom) in determining permissibility, allowing Muslims to adapt their social interactions with People of the Book based on prevailing cultural norms in their respective regions. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding social integration, provided the core tenets of faith are not compromised.
